description: JD-driven tutorial suggestion, gap analysis (76-band). Match the requirements extracted in 75 against what the library ALREADY teaches, classifying each requirement as covered / partially-covered / missing, and reusing the coverage model already written down in docs/gap-analysis.md. The corpus to match against is concrete and shipped: the 245 seed notebooks across 14 domains PLUS the `recommended`-tagged neighbours already enumerated in curriculum.py (T(..., recommended=True)) and catalogued in docs/gap-analysis.md §2 — a topic that is only scaffolded still counts as covered for suggestion purposes, because the point is to avoid re-tutorialing material the product can already build. This band produces the classification only; turning gaps into suggestions is band 77. Depends on 75. Anti-fabrication: coverage is computed from the real curriculum.py DOMAINS/topics (built live, not a hand-copied list), so it cannot drift from the shipped library; a test pins the domain/topic counts it reads.
warmup: echo '--- the shipped corpus: domains, topics, recommended tags ---'; grep -n 'DOMAINS\|def all_domains\|def all_topics\|recommended' curriculum.py | head -20
echo '--- the coverage model to reuse ---'; sed -n '1,60p' docs/gap-analysis.md

echo '--- reality: 14 domains, 245 notebooks ---'; python3 -c "import curriculum as c; print(len(c.DOMAINS),'domains'); print(sum(len(d.topics) for d in c.DOMAINS),'topics')" 2>/dev/null || find notebooks -name '*.ipynb' | wc -l

userStories.title: A library coverage index built live from the shipped curriculum
acceptanceCriteria: A module in the construction core builds the dedup corpus live from curriculum.py — every DOMAIN's topics across all 14 domains plus the `recommended`-tagged neighbours — rather than from any hand-copied list, so it tracks the real 245-notebook (14-domain) library and its recommended additions with no drift.

The index normalizes topic titles/slugs for matching in the same lenient spirit as the rest of the JD funnel (case/punctuation-insensitive, alias-tolerant) so a requirement phrased differently than the topic title can still match.

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ passes, including a test that asserts the index is built from curriculum.DOMAINS and that its domain/topic counts match the shipped library (guarding against a stale copy).

userStories.title: Classify each requirement covered / partial / missing
acceptanceCriteria: Given a requirement list from 75, each requirement is classified as covered (a shipped or recommended topic already teaches it), partially-covered (an adjacent topic touches it but is not a match), or missing (nothing in the library addresses it), reusing the covered/partial/missing coverage model of docs/gap-analysis.md.

Each classification carries the matched topic(s)/domain(s) as evidence so band 77 can attach a gap rationale, and a `recommended`-tagged neighbour counts as covered (it is already scaffolded — re-tutorialing it is exactly the redundancy this funnel must avoid).

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ covers a mixed requirement set asserting at least one covered, one partial, and one missing classification against the real library index, each with its evidence.
